notes.summary: A synonym is a word with the same or nearly the same meaning (candid = frank). SSC CGL Tier 1 asks 1 to 2 synonym questions and Tier 2 asks more. Most are a single word with four one-word options; the rest put the word in a sentence or ask you to fill a blank with the synonym of a bracketed word. Recall is fastest, but roots, part of speech, tone (good or bad sense) and elimination solve most unfamiliar words.

concepts.title: How SSC asks synonym questions
concepts.body:
• Given word: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. LUCID. About 3 in 5 questions look like this.
  • Word in a sentence: one word is underlined or bold. Read the whole sentence: the word may be used in a less common sense.
  • Bracket and blank: The doctor ______ (advised) rest. The answer must mean the bracketed word and fit the grammar of the blank (prescribed, not prescription).
  • Meaning of a word: options are short definitions, e.g. Lacuna: a gap or missing part.

concepts.title: A four-step method
concepts.body:
1. Say the meaning in your own words before reading the options.
  2. Match the part of speech. The synonym of an adjective is an adjective: diligent = industrious, not industry.
  3. Match the tone. Positive words have positive synonyms. Frugal (careful with money, a mild word) is closer to thrifty than to miserly (an insult).
  4. Eliminate the antonym (it is almost always in the options), look-alike words, and words that are only related in topic.

concepts.title: One word, several senses
concepts.body:
In sentence questions the meaning depends on the context. Read the sentence before choosing.
  • Grave: a grave mistake = serious; dug a grave = tomb.
  • Fair: a fair decision = just; fair skin = light; a trade fair = exhibition.
  • Check: check the answers = examine; check the spread of disease = control, curb.
  • Sound: sound advice = sensible; sound sleep = deep; safe and sound = unharmed.
  • Hard: hard work = tough; a hard surface = firm; hard-earned money = earned with effort.
  • Vogue: in vogue = in fashion, popular.

varieties.name: Synonym of a given word
varieties.how: Say the meaning in your own words, then pick the option with the same meaning, part of speech and tone. Strike out the antonym and look-alikes first.

example.q:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Benevolent
steps: bene = good, vol = wish: wishing good to others.
Options: Kind, Hostile, Cunning, Timid. Hostile is the opposite sense.
Only kind means wishing or doing good.

varieties.name: Synonym of a word in a sentence
varieties.how: Read the full sentence and decide what the word means here. Put each option into the sentence; the right one keeps the same meaning and grammar.

example.q:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
Narcotic drug addiction is in vogue these days, as it is the most popular form of substance abuse.
steps: in vogue = in fashion, popular. The sentence itself says most popular.
in fashion keeps the meaning; obscurity is the opposite.

varieties.name: Fill the blank with a synonym
varieties.how: Find the synonym of the bracketed word, then check it fits the blank in tense, number and part of speech.

example.q:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank.
The doctor has ______ (advised) medicine for the treatment of the disease.
steps: A doctor who advises medicine prescribes it.
Pick the V3 form: prescribed, not prescription or prescribe.

varieties.name: Meaning of a word
varieties.how: The options are short definitions. Match the definition, not a word that only sounds related.

example.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given word.
Lacuna
steps: Lacuna comes from Latin lacus (pool, hollow): an empty space.
Options: a gap or missing part; a small lake; a feeling of sadness; a type of tax.
a small lake is a root trap; the English word means a gap.

tips: Think of the meaning before you look at the options, so look-alike words cannot pull you.
Match part of speech: an adjective needs an adjective, a verb needs a verb.
Match the tone: a positive word has a positive synonym, a negative word a negative one.
The antonym is almost always one of the options. Cross it out first.
For a word in a sentence, plug each option into the sentence and read it again.
Learn roots (bene, mal, loqu, chron, cred) to guess unfamiliar words.
Revise 10 to 15 words a day with the flashcards; repetition beats long lists.
traps: Related but not equal: principle is a rule (axiom), not a headmaster.
Degree matters: frugal is closer to thrifty than to miserly.
In bracket-blank questions the right word in the wrong form (prescription for a verb blank) is still wrong.
Invaluable means priceless and inflammable means easily burnt; the prefix does not mean not here.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Candid
questions.solution: Candid means honest and straightforward = Frank. Secretive is close to its opposite.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Abundant
questions.solution: Abundant = existing in large quantities = Plentiful. Scarce is the antonym.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bold word.
Her meticulous notes made it easy for the team to repeat the experiment.
questions.solution: Notes that let others repeat an experiment must be very detailed and careful. Meticulous = Painstaking.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Loquacious

Select the most appropriate synonym of the bold word.
The committee's decision was arbitrary; no one could explain the reasons behind it.
questions.solution: A decision without explainable reasons is based on whim. Arbitrary = Capricious. Judicious (wise, well judged) is nearly the opposite.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Ephemeral
questions.solution: Ephemeral = lasting a very short time = Transient. Ethereal (delicate, heavenly) is a look-alike trap; Eternal is the antonym.
